newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Supreme Court postpones "dirty war" ruling.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Supreme Court postpones "dirty war" ruling.

text.p: MADRID, Jan 20 (Reuter - Spain's Supreme Court postponed on a decision on Monday over whether it will demand the government hand over secret files on a "dirty war" waged against Basque separatist rebels under the previous Socialist administration.

Lower courts are calling for the declassification of some 20 documents that give details of a secret campaign of assassinations and kidnappings against guerrillas of ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedome) in the 1980s.
The conservative Popular Party (PP) government, like the Socialist one before it, has refused, citing reasons of state security.
The Supreme Court said it would postpone its decision for 20 days to give it time to request and study more evidence.

Documents already leaked to the press suggest the Socialist government of Felipe Gonzalez was responsible for organising death squads known as the Anti-Terrorist Liberation Groups (GAL), which killed 28 people between 1983 and 1987.
